title: Symmetry-restored EXX density matrix double-divides by |star| (IBZ weight applied twice)
symptom: EXX bands from the symmetry path come out wrong in a state-dependent way; a naive constant-weight patch made the EXX gap explode 9.116 -> 57.54 eV.
root_cause: band_out occupations already encode IBZ geometric weights (w_root/50 = |star|/384), librpa.cpp divides by N_IBZ again, and Exx::get_dmat_cplx_R_symmetry_restored() multiplies by 1/|star| a third time: large star groups are systematically suppressed.
minimal_fix: Remove the 1/|star| factor in the symmetry-restored density matrix so the IBZ weight is applied exactly once; validate against a symmetry-off full-flow run of the same system.
validation: sym off (fresh ABACUS+LibRPA both ends) EXX gap 9.1232 eV vs sym on 9.1161 eV: 7.2 meV agreement is the acceptance bar.
avoid: Compensating with a constant N_IBZ/N_full rescale, or attributing the residual to symmetry itself.

parameters.check: sym on/off full-flow delta <= ~10 meV EXX gap
